answer.rationale: p99 latency is 5x target and confined to primary region during peak settlement traffic, 2 hours post-release. Regional failover (memory_b2) restored latency fast during March degradation with clean traffic shift and minutes-scale error recovery. Verifying memory_b1 to confirm rollback risk profile—if the recent release caused this, failover buys time for investigation while preserving writes; if not, failover still unblocks the primary region gracefully. Settlement peak means we cannot afford sustained 5x latency. Failover is reversible and has proven fast recovery. Circuit breakers and routing read replicas don't address write-path latency under heavy transactional load. Add capacity takes time we don't have at peak. Rollback introduces release cycle risk during peak writes.
